Assembly.information:
State representatives write, review and vote on legislation that becomes state law if approved by the Legislature and signed by the governor.
State representatives serve on one or more of 37 committees that take public testimony on bills and review legislation. 
They work on a state budget every other year to determine how tens of billions of dollars are spent.
State representatives also oversee a small staff that helps provide constituent services. Each member of the Assembly represents roughly 59,000 people.

Senate.information:
State senators write, review and vote on legislation that becomes state law if approved by the Legislature and signed by the governor.
They vet some political appointees made by the governor, including cabinet secretaries.
Senators serve on one or more of 20 committees that take public testimony on bills and review legislation. 
They work on a state budget every other year to determine how tens of billions of dollars are spent.
Senators also oversee a staff that helps provide constituent services. Each member of the state Senate represents roughly 175,000 people.

US Congress.information:
Members of Congress write, review and vote on legislation. Bills often move more quickly through the U.S. House than the U.S. Senate.
Representatives often serve on one or more committees where they hold information hearings, review legislation and sometimes conduct investigations. 
Congresspeople also oversee a staff, often maintaining both a Washington office and a district office in their home state.

Governor.information:
Wisconsin’s governor is the state’s top executive. The governor considers all bills approved by the Legislature and has the power to sign, veto, or, in the case of appropriation bills, partially veto proposed legislation that comes to their desk. They can also call the Legislature into special sessions and ask lawmakers to consider specific types of legislation. 
The governor appoints heads of executive agencies, such as the Department of Natural Resources, and many state boards and commissions. Most appointees require Senate confirmation. 
The governor can also make appointments to vacant judicial seats and county-level offices. 
Wisconsin’s governor has the power to pardon or grant clemency for individuals in the state’s criminal justice system.  
The governor is the commander in chief of the Wisconsin National Guard and can decide if and when to deploy soldiers.

races.district-race-nutshell: Republican U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany faces Andy Manske, a 27-year-old medical services technician from Greenfield, in the race to become the GOP gubernatorial nominee. Tiffany, who is endorsed by the Republican Party of Wisconsin and President Donald Trump, is favored to win the primary election. The winner will face the candidate that wins the six-way Democratic primary on Aug. 11.

After Democratic Gov. Tony Evers chose not to seek reelection this year, six candidates are running for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination. They include former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes, former Department of Administration Secretary Joel Brennan, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, Madison state Rep. Francesca Hong, Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez and Madison state Sen. Kelda Roys. The candidate that wins on Aug. 11 will face the winner of the Republican primary. Voters will see former Wisconsin Economic Development Corp. Secretary Missy Hughes on the ballot, but Hughes dropped out of the race in June and endorsed Rodriguez.

Attorney General.information:
The attorney general heads the Wisconsin Department of Justice, which provides legal advice and representation, investigates criminal activity, and provides various law enforcement services for the state. 
The attorney general is one of three members of the state’s Board of Commissioners of Public Lands along with the secretary of state and the state treasurer.

races.district-race-nutshell: The attorney general heads the Wisconsin Department of Justice, which provides legal advice and representation, investigates criminal activity, and provides various law enforcement services for the state. The race for attorney general is a rematch between the incumbent, Democrat Josh Kaul, and Republican Eric Toney, Fond du Lac County’s district attorney. In 2022, Kaul defeated Toney, 50.6% to 49.3%. Kaul won his first four-year term in 2018, defeating Republican incumbent Brad Schimel, 49.4% to 48.8%. Toney was first elected Fond du Lac county’s top prosecutor in 2012.

Lieutenant Gov.information:
The lieutenant governor serves as Wisconsin’s governor when there is a vacancy in the state’s top executive office.
The person takes on duties assigned by the governor, which can include serving on statutory or nonstatutory boards, committees or intergovernmental programs and coordinating state programs.

races.district-race-nutshell: The partisan primary is the chance for voters to individually choose their desired candidate for lieutenant governor, as the winning candidates from each party form a joint ballot with the gubernatorial nominees in the general election. Will Martin, a consultant from Racine, and David Varnam, a stay-at-home dad from Lancaster, face each other in the Republican primary for lieutenant governor. Martin is endorsed by the Republican Party of Wisconsin. The winner will join the ticket of the candidate that wins the Republican gubernatorial primary on Aug. 11. Sarah Godlewski, the current Secretary of State, is unopposed in the Democratic primary for lieutenant governor and will join the ticket of the winner of the Democratic gubernatorial primary.

Treasurer.information:
The treasurer signs checks and oversees the promotion of Wisconsin’s unclaimed property program. 
The treasurer is one of three members of the state’s Board of Commissioners of Public Lands along with the attorney general and the secretary of state.

races.district-race-nutshell: Dylan Helmenstine, a Black Earth village board trustee and Wisconsin Heights School Board member, faces Yee Leng Xiong, a Marathon County Supervisor and DC Everest School Board member, in the Democratic primary for state treasurer. The winner of the Aug. 11 election will face incumbent Republican State Treasurer John Leiber in the general election this November.

Secretary of State.information:
The secretary of state is Wisconsin’s official record keeper, which includes keeping track of enrolled laws, resolutions, official acts, fees, positions and appointments. They also maintain the state seal and add it to official acts taken by the governor. 
Unlike many other states, the Secretary of State does not administer Wisconsin’s elections. That power lies with local governments and the Wisconsin Elections Commission. 
The Secretary of State is one of three members of the state’s Board of Commissioners of Public Lands along with the attorney general and the state treasurer.

races.district-race-nutshell: It's a four-way race in the Republican primary for Secretary of State, which will determine who will advance to the general election in November. The candidates include Brayden Myer of Manitowoc, Nate Pollnow of the Town of Elba, Jay Schroeder of XXXX and Cindy Werner of Milwaukee. Pollnow, who is endorsed by the Republican Party of Wisconsin, is the likely favorite.   The winner of the Republican primary will face Democrat JoCasta Zamarripa, a Milwaukee alderwoman, and Green Party candidate Pete Karas, a retired small business owner in Muskego.
